findings.reason: without an edge one of the two nodes's edits to those log sites is lost at merge or comes back as a repair round the plan did not budget.
findings.text: §2 declares `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py` as a write path while §6 declares the same file (plan.html:82) and neither the `plan-section-depends-on` map nor followup f-awojcosf-001, which says "§6 and §8 are independent of them and of each other", orders them, so two nodes the plan calls independent edit one module concurrently.

findings.reason: the section's measure would go green while the defect it exists to stop survives, and "with truncating open restored" cannot be applied to a runner that does not truncate.
findings.text: §6's done-when measures only the absence of a truncating open, but the truncating mode is not the whole exposure: `reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:922,932` append (`open("a")`) and `reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py` never writes a log through the named path, and an append open follows a symlink and creates a dangling target exactly as `"w"` does, so a tree that passes the grep still replays the incident through the append runner.

findings.reason: the section should declare the delivered record — a gate log the run created, no caller-supplied path, manifest gate fields a promotion check accepts — and leave the verb choice to the node, so a wrong guess about which verbs qualify does not cost a review round.
findings.text: §7's deliverable fixes a method and an interface ("The two gate verbs ... are extended ...; no new verb is added;" plus "a dispatched worker's prompt carries the composed call"), which is the reuse map a node brief composes, not an endpoint a plan should state.
